label: sto_wave_phi
title: Example
body_md:
\label{sto_wave_phi}
For the stochastic wave motion, the stochastic field-theoretic equations \eqref{e8}-\eqref{e7} and \eqref{e9} specialize to
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&d_{t}\mu = - \sigma_{s}dt - \frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta \phi}\circ dW, 
\quad
d_{t}\phi = \zeta dt + \frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}\circ dW, 
\quad
\phi_{s} = \gamma,\\
&\mu = \zeta, 
\quad
\sigma = -\gamma, 
\quad
d_{t}\gamma = \zeta_{s}dt + \partial_{s}\left(\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}\right)\circ dW.
\label{wave_2_1}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
In particular, if the stochastic potential $\Phi = \phi$, the stochastic field-theoretic equations \eqref{wave_2_1} become, in components,
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{d}_{t}\zeta = \Delta\phi \mathrm{d}t - \mathrm{d}W, 
\quad
\mathrm{d}_{t}\phi = \zeta \mathrm{d}t, 
\quad
\mathrm{d}_{t}\phi_{s} = \zeta_{s}\mathrm{d}t,
\end{align*}
which recovers the stochastic linear wave equations with additive noise in \cite{HoSu2022}. Furthermore, if $\Phi$ is chosen to be zero, equations \eqref{wave_2_1} become
\begin{align*}
\mu_{t} = - \sigma_{s}, 
\quad
\phi_{t} = \zeta, 
\quad
\phi_{s} = \gamma,
\quad
\mu = \zeta, 
\quad
\sigma = -\gamma, 
\quad
\gamma_{t} = \zeta_{s},
\end{align*}
which recovers the deterministic wave equation \citep{evans2022partial}.

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{Coro_Energy}
If the Hamiltonian $h$ Poisson-commutes with the stochastic potential $\Phi$, that is, $\left\{h,\Phi\right\} = 0$, then the total energy of the stochastic system is a conserved quantity.

title: Proof
body_md:
By taking the variation of \eqref{action_sum} and using \eqref{approx_variation_Type_2}, we have
\begin{align*}
\delta A_{d}
&= \sum_{n=1}^{N-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}
\left[
\Delta t\Delta s\left<\frac{\delta\ell}{\delta g}\left(g^{n}_{j}, \zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}, \gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}\right), \delta g^{n}_{j}\right>
+
\Delta t\Delta s\left<\frac{\delta\ell}{\delta\zeta}\left(g^{n}_{j}, \zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}, \gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}\right), \delta\zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}\right>  \right.  \\
&\qquad
+
\Delta t\Delta s\left<\frac{\delta\ell}{\delta\gamma}\left(g^{n}_{j}, \zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}, \gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}\right), \delta\gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}\right>
+
\left<\delta\mu^{n+1/2}_{j}, 
\tau^{-1}\left(\left(g^{n}_{j}\right)^{-1}g^{n+1}_{j}\right)
- \Delta t\zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}\right>\Delta s  \\
&\qquad
+
\left<\mu^{n+1/2}_{j}, 
\eta^{n+1}_{j} - \eta^{n}_{j}
+ \left[
\tau^{-1}\left(\left(g^{n}_{j}\right)^{-1}g^{n+1}_{j}\right), \eta^{n+1/2}_{j}
\right]
- \Delta t\delta\zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}\right>\Delta s  \\
&\qquad
+
\left<\delta\sigma^{n}_{j}, 
\tau^{-1}\left(\left(g^{n}_{j}\right)^{-1}g^{n}_{j+1}\right)
- \Delta s\gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}\right>\Delta t  \\
&\qquad
+
\left<\sigma^{n}_{j+1/2}, \eta^{n}_{j+1} - \eta^{n}_{j}
+ \left[
\tau^{-1}\left(\left(g^{n}_{j}\right)^{-1}g^{n}_{j+1}\right), \eta^{n}_{j+1/2}
\right]
- \Delta s\delta\gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}\right>\Delta t  \\
&\qquad \left.
-
\Delta s
\left(
\left<\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta g}\left(g^{n}_{j}, \mu^{n+1/2}_{j}\right), \delta g^{n}_{j}\right>
+ \left<\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta \mu}\left(g^{n}_{j}, \mu^{n+1/2}_{j}\right), \delta \mu^{n+1/2}_{j}\right>
\right)
\left(
W^{(M)}_{n+1,j} - W^{(M)}_{n,j}
\right)
\right]  \\
& + \text{Boundary terms},
\end{align*}
where we have rearranged the indices $n$ and $j$. By the boundary condition $\delta g^{0}_{j} = \delta g^{N}_{j} = 0$, $j=1,...,J$, (or equivalently $\eta^{0}_{j} = \eta^{N}_{j} = 0$, $j=1,...,J$), and the arbitrariness of $\delta\zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}$, $\delta\gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}$, $\delta\mu^{n+1/2}_{j}$, and $\delta\sigma^{n}_{j+1/2}$, we obtain the desired result.

title: Example
body_md:
The type-II stochastic integrator \eqref{dis_tem_eqn_2}-\eqref{dis_compatibility_2} for the stochastic wave system becomes
\begin{align*}
&
\Delta s \left(\mu^{n-1/2}_{j} - \mu^{n+1/2}_{j}\right)
+ \left(\sigma^{n}_{j-1/2} - \sigma^{n}_{j+1/2}\right)\Delta t
- \Delta s\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\phi}\left(\phi^{n}_{j},\mu^{n+1/2}_{j}\right)
\left(
W^{(M)}_{n+1,j} - W^{(M)}_{n,j}
\right)
= 0, \\
&\Delta s\left(\gamma^{n+1}_{j+1/2} - \gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}\right)
- \Delta t\left(\zeta^{n+1/2}_{j+1} - \zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}\right)  \\
&\quad
+ \frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}\left(\phi^{n}_{j},\mu^{n+1/2}_{j}\right)
\left(W^{(M)}_{n+1,j} - W^{(M)}_{n,j}\right)
-  \frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}\left(\phi^{n}_{j+1},\mu^{n+1/2}_{j+1}\right)
\left(W^{(M)}_{n+1,j+1} - W^{(M)}_{n,j+1}\right) = 0,  \\
&\phi^{n+1}_{j} - \phi^{n}_{j}
- \Delta t\zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}
- \frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}\left(\phi^{n}_{j},\mu^{n+1/2}_{j}\right)
\left(
W^{(M)}_{n+1,j} - W^{(M)}_{n,j}
\right) = 0, \\
&\phi^{n}_{j+1} - \phi^{n}_{j}
- \Delta s\gamma^{n}_{j+1/2} = 0, \\
&\mu^{n+1/2}_{j} = \zeta^{n+1/2}_{j}, \\
&\sigma^{n}_{j+1/2} = - \gamma^{n}_{j+1/2}, \\
&
\gamma^{n}_{1/2} = \gamma^{n}_{J+1/2} = 0.
\end{align*}
In particular, when the stochastic potential $\Phi$ is taken to be zero, the above integrator specializes to the well-known Yee's scheme \citep{Yee1966} in the deterministic setting.

title: Proof
body_md:
Using the Stratonovich chain rule and \eqref{sto_Hamel_Ham}-\eqref{sto_com_Ham}, we have
\begin{align*}
d_{t}f(\gamma,\mu) &= \left<\frac{\delta f}{\delta\gamma},d_{t}\gamma\right> + \left<d_{t}\mu, \frac{\delta f}{\delta\mu}\right> \\
&=
\left<
\frac{\delta f}{\delta\gamma},
\left(
\frac{\partial}{\partial s}\frac{\delta h}{\delta\mu}
+ \mathrm{ad}_{\gamma}\frac{\delta h}{\delta\mu}
\right)dt
+ \left(
\mathrm{ad}_{\gamma}\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}
+ \frac{\partial}{\partial s}\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}
\right)\circ dW
\right>  \\
&\quad
+
\left<
\left(
\mathrm{ad}^{*}_{\frac{\delta h}{\delta\mu}}\mu
+ \frac{\partial}{\partial s}\frac{\delta h}{\delta\gamma}
- \mathrm{ad}^{*}_{\gamma}\frac{\delta h}{\delta\gamma}
\right)dt
+ \mathrm{ad}^{*}_{\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}}\mu\circ dW,
\frac{\delta f}{\delta\mu}
\right>  \\
&=
\left(
\left<
\frac{\delta f}{\delta\gamma},
\frac{\partial}{\partial s}\frac{\delta h}{\delta\mu} 
+ \mathrm{ad}_{\gamma}\frac{\delta h}{\delta\mu}
\right>
+
\left<
\mathrm{ad}^{*}_{\frac{\delta h}{\delta\mu}}\mu
+ \frac{\partial}{\partial s}\frac{\delta h}{\delta\gamma}
- \mathrm{ad}^{*}_{\gamma}\frac{\delta h}{\delta\gamma},
\frac{\delta f}{\delta\mu}
\right>
\right)dt  \\
&\quad
+
\left(
\left<
\frac{\delta f}{\delta\gamma},
\mathrm{ad}_{\gamma}\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}
+ \frac{\partial}{\partial s}\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}
\right>
+
\left<
\mathrm{ad}^{*}_{\frac{\delta\Phi}{\delta\mu}}\mu,
\frac{\delta f}{\delta\mu}
\right>
\right)\circ dW  \\
&=
\left\{f,h\right\}dt + \left\{f,\Phi\right\}\circ dW,
\end{align*}
where the last equality follows from Lemma~\ref{ChenShi2025}.

To prove the converse, we take $f=\gamma$ and $f=\mu$ in \eqref{SLP}, respectively. Then, it is straightforward to obtain the stochastic field-theoretic equation \eqref{sto_Hamel_Ham} and the stochastic compatibility condition \eqref{sto_com_Ham} in Hamiltonian forms.  \hfill $\Box$
